lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
بَشَّرَ bashshara [v. II, trans.]

1 to bring good tidings, to convey good news

(10:2) وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ and give glad news to those who believe, that they are on a sure footing with their Lord

2 (ironically) to bring bad tidings

(9:34) وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلاَ يُنْفِقُونَهَا فِى سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ those who treasure up gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God, give them the bad [lit. good] tidings of a painful chastisement.

بَشَّرَ bashshara 35 times; بُشِّرَ bushshira 3 times; تُبَاشِرُ tubāshir 2 times; أَبْشِرْ ʾabshir 1 time; تَسْتَبْشِرُون tastabshirūn 7 times; بُشْرَى bushrā 18 times; بَشِيرٌ bashır 9 times; مُبَشِّرٌ mubashshir 5 times; مُبَشِّرِين mubashshirın 4 times; مُبَشِّرَاتٌ mubashshirāt 1 time; مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ mustabshiratun 1 time; بَشَرٌ bashar 36 times and بَشْرَينِ bashrayn 1 time.

entries.label: بَشَّرَ
entries.definitionHtml:
بَشَّرَ bashshara [v. II, trans.]

1 to bring good tidings, to convey good news

(10:2) وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ and give glad news to those who believe, that they are on a sure footing with their Lord

2 (ironically) to bring bad tidings

(9:34) وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلاَ يُنْفِقُونَهَا فِى سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ those who treasure up gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God, give them the bad [lit. good] tidings of a painful chastisement.

entries.label: أَبْشِرْ
entries.definitionHtml:
أَبْشِرْ ʾabshir [imper. of v. IV أَبْشَرَ ʾabshara, intrans.] to feel joy at receiving good news

(41:30) وَأَبْشِرُوا بِالْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ and rejoice at the good news of [your entering] Paradise, that you have been promised.

entries.label: بَشَرٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
بَشَرٌ bashar I [collect. n. equally applied to masc. and fem.; sing. and pl.] humankind

(30:20) وَمِنْ ءَايَاتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ إِذَا أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ تَنْتَشِرُونَ of His wonders is His creating you from dust, and Lo and behold, you became human beings, multiplying/spreading II [n.; dual بَشَرَينِ basharayn] human

(23:47) فَقَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَيْنِ مِثْلِنَا they said, ‘Are we to believe in two human beings like us?’ III [pl. of بشرة basharatun/coll. n.] skin (in an interpretation of verse 74:29) لَوَّاحَةٌ لِلْبَشَرِ blackening the skins (or, scorching the flesh of humans).

entries.label: بَشِيرٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
بَشِيرٌ bashır [n.] a bearer of good tidings

(12:96) فَلَمَّا أَنْ جَاءَ الْبَشِيرُ أَلْقَاهُ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ فَارْتَدَّ بَصِيرًا then, when the bearer of good news came and placed it onto his face, thereupon he became able to see again.

entries.label: بُشِّرَ
entries.definitionHtml:
بُشِّرَ bushshira [pass. of v. II] to be given good news (and ironically bad news)

(16:58) وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِالأُنْثَى ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ when one of them is given the good news of [the birth of] a baby girl, his face darkens and he is filled with gloom.

entries.label: بُشْرَى
entries.definitionHtml:
بُشْرَى bushrā [n.] glad tidings, good news

(39:17) وَالَّذِينَ اجْتَنَبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوهَا وَأَنَابُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ لَهُمُ الْبُشْرَى there is good news for those who shun the worship of false gods and turn to God; *

(12:19) يَابُشْرَى how fortunate!, what good news! [also: يَا بُشْرَايَ how fortunate I am!, what good news for me!]; *

(57:12) بُشْرَاكُمُ good news for you.

entries.label: تُبَاشِرُ
entries.definitionHtml:
تُبَاشِرُ tubāshir [imperf. of v. III بَاشَرَ bāshara, trans.] euphemism for being intimate with one’s wife (to be in skin‐to‐skin contact)

(2:187) وَلاَ تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنْتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِى الْمَسَاجِدِ but do not lie with them [your wives] during the nights of your devotional retreat in the mosques.

entries.label: مُبَشِّرٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
مُبَشِّرٌ mubashshir [act. part.; pl. مُبَشِّرِين mubashshirın; pl. fem. مُبَشِّرَاتٌ mubashshirāt] one who brings good news

(30:46) وَمِنْ ءَايَاتِهِ أَنْ يُرْسِلَ الرِّيَاحَ مُبَشِّرَاتٍ His wonders include sending out the winds bearing good news.

entries.label: مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ mustabshiratun [act. part. fem.] one who rejoices at receiving or expecting good news

(80:39) ضَاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ laughing and expectantly rejoicing [at what is coming].

entries.label: يَسْتَبْشِرُون
entries.definitionHtml:
يَسْتَبْشِرُون yastabshirūn [imperf. of v. X اسْتَبْشَرَ ʾistabshara, intrans.]

1 to be happy, content, or joyful at receiving good news

(9:111) فَاسْتَبْشِرُوا بِبَيْعِكُمُ الَّذِي بَايَعْتُمْ بِهِ so rejoice in the bargain you have made [with God]

2 to be happy at the thought of expected good happening,

(3:171) يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ they rejoice at the thought of receiving God’s blessing and favour

3 to seek good tidings

(15:67) وَجَاءَ أَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ the people of the town came along seeking the good tidings [of possible pleasure].
